title: Ceva's Theorem at Arbitrary Curvature κ via the Curvature Sine
description: The parent (cevas-theorem-non-euclidean) proves Ceva's theorem in Euclidean, spherical, and hyperbolic geometry, unified through an arbitrary distance function ρ. This entry answers its OQ-01: extend the unified framework to arbitrary curvature κ using the curvature sine sin_κ. We define sin_κ(x) = sin(√κ·x)/√κ (κ>0), x (κ=0), sinh(√(−κ)·x)/√(−κ) (κ<0), prove it specializes to sin/sinh/identity at κ = 1/−1/0, and prove a single curvature-parametrised Ceva theorem by instantiating the parent's ceva_unified_principle at ρ = sin_κ. The classical spherical, hyperbolic, and Euclidean Ceva conditions fall out as the three cases.

overview.historicalContext:
Ceva's theorem characterizes when three cevians of a triangle are concurrent: in the Euclidean plane, AD, BE, CF meet at a point iff (BD/DC)·(CE/EA)·(AF/FB) = 1. The theorem has clean analogues in spherical geometry (with the segment lengths replaced by their sines) and in hyperbolic geometry (replaced by hyperbolic sines). These three statements are unified by the notion of constant curvature κ: spherical geometry has κ > 0, Euclidean κ = 0, hyperbolic κ < 0, and the natural 'length' to use is the curvature sine sin_κ, which equals sin(√κ·x)/√κ, x, or sinh(√(−κ)·x)/√(−κ) according to the sign of κ.

The parent gallery entry proved the three cases separately and abstracted their common algebraic core into ceva_unified_principle, which works for an arbitrary positive 'distance function' ρ. What it did not provide is the specific geometric interpolant sin_κ tying ρ to the curvature κ. This entry supplies sin_κ, proves it specializes to the three classical distance functions, and feeds it into the parent's principle to obtain a single theorem valid at every curvature.
overview.problemStatement: Define the curvature sine sin_κ and prove the unified curvature-κ Ceva theorem: for any κ, three cevians of a geodesic triangle in the curvature-κ geometry are concurrent iff (sin_κ(BD)/sin_κ(DC))·(sin_κ(CE)/sin_κ(EA))·(sin_κ(AF)/sin_κ(FB)) = 1. Show this recovers the spherical (sin), hyperbolic (sinh), and Euclidean (length) conditions at κ = 1, −1, 0.
overview.proofStrategy: Define sin_κ by cases on the sign of κ. The specializations sin_κ=1 ↦ sin, κ=−1 ↦ sinh, κ=0 ↦ id follow by reducing the if-then-else (with √1 = 1). Positivity sin_κ(x) > 0 for x > 0 splits on sign: spherical uses sin_pos_of_pos_of_lt_pi with √κ·x < π, hyperbolic uses sinh_pos_of_pos, Euclidean is x > 0 directly. The unified theorem kappa_ceva is a direct instantiation of the parent's ceva_unified_principle at ρ = sin_κ. The three geometric corollaries rewrite sin_κ via its specialization lemmas.
keyInsights: Curvature is a single real parameter κ, and the right 'length' for Ceva at curvature κ is the curvature sine sin_κ — one function that becomes sin, identity, or sinh according to the sign of κ.

The unified Ceva theorem at arbitrary κ is not new algebra: it is the parent's ceva_unified_principle (the cross-multiplication identity) applied to ρ = sin_κ. The geometry is entirely encoded in the choice of distance function.

The √κ normalization in sin_κ cancels inside the ratios of the Ceva condition, so the concurrency criterion has the same form in every geometry — only the function applied to the segment lengths changes.

The spherical case carries a genuine constraint (√κ·x < π: segments shorter than half a great circle) needed for positivity, while the hyperbolic and Euclidean cases are unconditional — reflecting that great circles close up but hyperbolic/Euclidean geodesics do not.
Recovering the three classical theorems as κ = 1, −1, 0 confirms the curvature sine is the correct interpolant and exhibits the parent's three separate results as one.

conclusion.summary: A fully verified (0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide) extension, in 128 lines with 8 theorems, of the unified Ceva framework to arbitrary curvature κ. The curvature sine sin_κ is defined and shown to specialize to sin, sinh, and the identity at κ = 1, −1, 0; the single theorem kappa_ceva instantiates the parent's ceva_unified_principle at ρ = sin_κ, and the classical spherical, hyperbolic, and Euclidean Ceva conditions are recovered as the three cases.
conclusion.implications: This answers the parent's OQ-01: the unified Ceva framework does extend to arbitrary curvature κ via the curvature sine, and the extension is clean because the geometry is captured entirely by the choice ρ = sin_κ. It exhibits the three classical theorems as facets of one curvature-parametrised statement, and the sin_κ definition with its specialization and positivity lemmas is a reusable interpolant for other non-Euclidean concurrence results (e.g. a curvature-κ Menelaus or angle-bisector theorem).

Use sin_κ to formalize the curvature-κ Menelaus theorem and other concurrence/collinearity results in the same unified framework.
